action.content: What are the best things to do in Rochester, New York? Can you write them as a song and use music notation in your response? Make sure to include the keywords 'festival' and 'river'.
action.label: context

action.content:
\version "2.22.1"
\paper {
  #(set-paper-size "letter")
  top-margin = 15
  bottom-margin = 15
  left-margin = 15
  right-margin = 15
}

\header {
  title = "The Flower City Waltz"
  tagline = ##f
}

global = {
  \key g \major
  \time 3/4
  \tempo "Andante" 4 = 90
}

melody = \relative c' {
  \global
  % Verse 1: The Genesee River
  g4. e8 d4 | c4 bes4 a4 | g4. e8 d4 | c4 r4 r4 |
  % Chorus: The Festival
  g4. a8 bes4 | c4 d4 e4 | d4. c8 bes4 | a4 g4 r4 |
  % Verse 2: The Strong National Library
  g4. a8 bes4 | c4 d4 e4 | d4. c8 bes4 | a4 g4 r4 |
  % Outro
  g2. | g2. |
}

lyrics = \lyricmode {
  Walk -- ing down by the Gen -- ee -- se \river,
  Where the wa -- ter flows so free.
  See the falls and the his -- to -- ry,
  In the heart of the city.
  
  Join the crowd at the \fes -- ti -- val,
  Where the mu -- sic starts to play.
  Taste the food and see the art,
  In the light of the day.
  
  Read the books in the li -- brary,
  Where the knowl -- edge is so deep.
  Then go up to the park -- way,
  While the world is fast asleep.
  
  Roch -- es -- ter, Roch -- es -- ter,
  Roch -- es -- ter, Roch -- es -- ter.
}

\score {
  <<
    \new Staff \with { instrumentName = "Piano" } <<
      \new Voice = "melody" { \melody }
      \new ChordNames { \chordmode {
        g1 | c | g | c |
        g | c | g | c |
        g | c | g | c |
        g1 | g1 |
      }}
    >>
    \new Lyrics \lyricsto "melody" \lyrics
  >>
  \layout { }
}
action.label: response
